youtube.baslik: Does a bone-conduction dip always come from the inner ear? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In otosclerosis, bone conduction can drop around 2000 Hz, usually by about 15 dB; this is called the Carhart notch. It is not a true cochlear loss but a mechanical middle ear effect, and it often improves after successful stapes surgery.

sahneler.metin: Does a bone-conduction dip *always* mean inner ear?
cumleler: Does a bone-conduction dip always come from the inner ear?
In otosclerosis, bone conduction can drop around two thousand hertz.
The dip is usually about fifteen decibels: the Carhart notch.
This is not a true cochlear loss, but a mechanical effect.
It often improves after successful stapes surgery.
